scenario: an at-home diagnostic test kit platform tracking kit shipped and results released
title: Count High-Value Results by Kit Type
prompt: You manage an at-home diagnostic test kit platform. Each `kit_type` record represents a diagnostic test category (vitamin panel, allergy screen, etc.). The `result_release` table records every time a patient's test results were released, including the `price_paid` for that specific test. Write a query that lists every kit type alongside the count of result releases where the patient paid MORE THAN $75. Some kit types may have had no high-value releases, or no releases at all; those kit types must still appear in the output with a count of 0. Return columns `kit_type_id`, `kit_name`, and `high_value_count`, ordered by `kit_type_id` ascending. The filter on price_paid belongs to the result_release table (the right side of the join); ensure your join structure keeps every kit_type row regardless of whether it has any qualifying result releases.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE kit_type (kit_type_id INT PRIMARY KEY, kit_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL); CREATE TABLE result_release (release_id INT PRIMARY KEY, kit_type_id INT NOT NULL, patient_email VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL, price_paid DECIMAL(10,2) NOT NULL, released_at TIMESTAMP NOT NULL);
answer_key: SELECT kt.kit_type_id, kt.kit_name, COUNT(r.release_id) AS high_value_count FROM kit_type kt LEFT JOIN result_release r ON kt.kit_type_id = r.kit_type_id AND r.price_paid > 75 GROUP BY kt.kit_type_id, kt.kit_name ORDER BY kt.kit_type_id;
user_solution:
/*
Write a query that lists every kit type alongside the count of result releases where the patient paid MORE THAN $75.
Some kit types may have had no high-value releases, or no releases at all; those kit types must still appear in the output with a count of 0.
Return columns `kit_type_id`, `kit_name`, and `high_value_count`, ordered by `kit_type_id` ascending.
*/
SELECT
    k.kit_type_id,
    k.kit_name,
    CASE WHEN MAX(r.price_paid) > 75 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS high_value_count
FROM kit_type AS k
LEFT JOIN result_release AS r
ON k.kit_type_id = r.kit_type_id
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1;
